CVE-2026-99049.title: gpio: xilinx: fix runtime PM leak on request error path
CVE-2026-99049.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

gpio: xilinx: fix runtime PM leak on request error path

pm_runtime_get_sync() leaves the usage counter incremented even when it
fails, and xgpio_request() returns the error without dropping it.

gpiolib does not call ->free() when ->request() fails, so xgpio_free(),
which holds the only matching pm_runtime_put(), never runs. The reference
is leaked and the controller can no longer runtime-suspend, so its clock
stays enabled.

Switch to pm_runtime_resume_and_get(), which only increments the usage
counter on success.

CVE-2026-99401.title: rtnetlink: wait for RCU readers in rtnl_link_unregister()
CVE-2026-99401.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

rtnetlink: wait for RCU readers in rtnl_link_unregister()

rtnl_link_ops_get() finds ops on link_ops under rcu_read_lock() and only
then takes ops->srcu. rtnl_link_unregister() unlinks ops, then calls
synchronize_srcu() and cleanup_srcu_struct() without first waiting for
RCU readers. A reader that found ops before list_del_rcu() and has not yet
taken ops->srcu is not waited for.

Such a reader then locks a cleaned-up srcu_struct and keeps using ops
after the module that owns it is gone. rtnl_newlink() and
rtnl_dump_ifinfo() both look up ops without RTNL, the latter for any
user that dumps links filtered by kind.

With delays added between the lookup and srcu_read_lock() in
rtnl_link_ops_get(), and before rtnl_link_ops_put() in
rtnl_dump_ifinfo(), running "ip link show type dummy" alongside
"rmmod dummy" on a KASAN kernel gives:

Read of size 8 at addr…

CVE-2026-99474.title: HID: hiddev: keep state alive through disconnect unlock
CVE-2026-99474.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

HID: hiddev: keep state alive through disconnect unlock

mutex_unlock() clears the mutex owner before taking its wait lock. A
thread spinning in the final hiddev file release can acquire
existancelock after hiddev_disconnect() clears the owner, then free
hiddev before the disconnecting thread reaches the mutex wait lock. This
causes a use-after-free in the mutex slow unlock path.

Give the connection and each open file an explicit reference. Drop each
reference only after its existancelock critical section has completed,
so neither unlock path can free the mutex while the other is still using
it.

CVE-2026-99610.title: ALSA: caiaq: free the EP4 URB when input setup fails
CVE-2026-99610.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: caiaq: free the EP4 URB when input setup fails

The three controllers that use the EP4 input URB allocate it before
checking the endpoint type and before registering the input device. On
failure they jump to exit_free_idev, which clears cdev->input_dev but
leaves cdev->ep4_in_urb set. The card teardown then calls
snd_usb_caiaq_input_free(), which returns early because input_dev is
NULL, so the URB is never freed.

Release the URB before dropping the input device on the error path.
